nodes.label: F70-0001
nodes.text: in my view it's a really great car.

nodes.label: F70-0002
nodes.text: really solid build, lots of attention to detail. i only knock off one mark because there's no paper user manual.

nodes.label: F70-0003
nodes.text: the m135 xdrive is a joy to drive, powerful and feels safe. it is a very good looking car and extremely comfortable inside. i've had lots of different cars over the years but this one is definitely the best.

nodes.label: F70-0004
nodes.text: i've always been a big fan of the brand, starting with my first bmw, a used e46 320i coupe back in 2007, then an e83 x3 2.5i, before working in the bmw retailer network as a parts manager and later an aftersales manager, driving lots of company cars over the years, my favourite being the g21 m340d. after getting my wife an f56 cooper sport as her first car a couple of years ago, when it was time to change, the new 1 series was the obvious choice. she absolutely loves it and now understands why i've always said bmw will always be the best brand. james and the team at northbridge bmw chester were fantastic and turned her first new bmw handover into an experience she'll remember.

nodes.label: F70-0005
nodes.text:
offers a great balance of comfort and sport, ideal for anyone wanting that mix.
i do feel the assist motor power could be just a bit stronger!

nodes.label: F70-0006
nodes.text: its a lovely car, but a car is a very personal decision. if someone asked me, id say i recommend it, but i wouldnt bring it up on my own.

nodes.label: F70-0007
nodes.text: i was driving a golf 7.5 before and felt it was more stable and better to operate than local cars, but the 120 takes stability even further. i can tell that its rigidity and its quietness are key parts of those fundamentals.

nodes.label: F70-0008
nodes.text: very good to drive and the extra driver safety tech is very useful. the only frustration is not being able to turn off auto stop start for good, i have to cancel it on every start. please advise if there is a way to set this permanently. thanks

nodes.label: F70-0009
nodes.text: nice little car but it did take me a fair while to get my head around all the tech, i prefer things very plain and simple and as an older driver it felt a bit of a slog at the start. i specced the car with almost every extra i could get, as thats what i tend to do. now i am really pleased with it, the way it clings to the road is like a limpet and the steering gives loads of feedback, it almost feels like the car is talking to me and i always feel totally in control. over the years ive had around seven bmws, mostly three series and a couple of x2, and this one is every bit as good as those.

nodes.label: F70-0010
nodes.text: its a really good car, definitely feels like an upgrade over my old f40 118i m sport. engine is strong and the mild hybrid gives a nice extra shove and helps with efficiency. it corners and rides very well and im getting better fuel economy than with the f40. some of the cabin materials feel a bit flimsier than before, not a big deal but i did notice. the new cabin layout looks great and all the digital stuff behaves properly. a few oddities though: the keyless entry/exit reacts way too easily, and sometimes the car systems seem to randomly reset, so auto hold ends up switched off in the menu even though i had it on. the speed warning feature is just irritating, even if i can switch it off each trip here in the uk.

nodes.label: F70-0011
nodes.text:
fuel efficient and economical
quiet on the move and simple to drive.
its a design i dont get tired of
would prefer a dial for operating the screen
also think its better to have a muffler

nodes.label: F70-0012
nodes.text: the car drives nicely, is comfy, engine feels strong and the steering is quite light, but getting used to all the touchscreen tech is a nightmare. the previous idrive setup was almost perfect and should have been left alone. for example, getting the preset radio stations back onto the display is almost impossible, and being forced to use a touchscreen while driving is a dangerous distraction. there is no proper written owners manual, just loads of videos, which is disappointing as even a simple booklet would have helped. not being able to choose run flat tyres is a step backwards, and with no spare tyre that could be dangerous.

nodes.label: F70-0013
nodes.text: i'm really pleased with the upgrades on my new 1 series. the suspension and handling feel more refined. the small changes in the software and how the digital system works make it simpler to carry out the basic things.

nodes.label: F70-0014
nodes.text: the car itself is very good, but the electronic stuff just doesn't work well for us oldeer people.

nodes.label: F70-0015
nodes.text: the build quality seems not great; my seat has squeaks that i only noticed after turning my music off due to a damaged speaker. very frustrating to deal with both issues.

nodes.label: F70-0016
nodes.text: compact and very nimble car.

nodes.label: F70-0017
nodes.text: the harman kardon is really very poor, and there is too much tech with too few proper buttons and knobs for key functions. the vent controls are awkward to operate. i was so disappointed with this car that i ended up selling it after only 2 months, taking a big financial loss.

nodes.label: F70-0018
nodes.text: overall the car is very good, drives nicely, feels comfortable and looks smart. however, using the touch screen for various controls is awkward and far too complicated. the car actually broke down in the first two weeks of ownership and then needed nearly three weeks to be repaired, which is very disappointing for a new vehicle and below what i'd expect from bmw.

nodes.label: F70-0019
nodes.text:
driving feel that makes you forget its front wheel drive.
comes fully loaded with on-board gear.

nodes.label: F70-0020
nodes.text: you travel nicely, with safety and a luxurios feel.

nodes.label: F70-0021
nodes.text: looks superb, great driveability and performance, good economy, and the interior comfort with the m front seats. the options i picked when buying plus the driver aids all help, i really enjoy driving this car.

nodes.label: F70-0022
nodes.text: i'm mostly pleased with the car except for the satellite navigation. when we use it, it has taken us down tiny lanes that are only just wide enough for one vehicle so you can't get past anything coming the other way. this has happened on three trips and led to hold-ups and a lot of stress. my last 1 series let me pick between the fastest route and the shortest one but this new model doesn't offer that choice. i checked with the dealer and they confirmed this. i've chatted to other bmw drivers and they no longer rely on the idrive navigation, they just use their phones. i went for bmw as a premium brand but i'm really unhappy that the sat nav is basically not fit for purpose. simon fairclough [EMAIL]

nodes.label: F70-0023
nodes.text: the mileage is good and the interior is also good.

nodes.label: F70-0024
nodes.text: smoothness and satisfaction

nodes.label: F70-0025
nodes.text: the car is fantastic to drive. it's my first automatic and it's incredibly easy to use. i'm very happy with it.

nodes.label: F70-0026
nodes.text: in my view it is a very highly recommended car, especially for people who really love cars.

nodes.label: F70-0027
nodes.text: the car drives very well and has some lovely features, however i've had problems with both display modules going totally blank several times, always when the outside temperature is under zero degrees. the vehicle is currently with the local dealer for checks and repair.

nodes.label: F70-0028
nodes.text: this is my 4th bmw 1 series and easily the best to drive. the mild hybrid setup is excellent, same with the automatic gearbox. i have already done around a 1000 mile round trip to france in great comfort and with superb fuel economy.

nodes.label: F70-0029
nodes.text: the vehicle is lacking some features that the salesperson had told me would be included.

nodes.label: F70-0030
nodes.text: really nice to drive, feels secure with loads of grip on the road. seats are comfy and supportive, shame there isnt any lumbar support. infotainment is decent but ive hit a few issues. tivo keeps saying no connection and asking to retry, started happening after my annual subscription kicked in.

nodes.label: F70-0031
nodes.text: front seats dont give the support they should. brakes feel very unprogressive, either doing nothing or suddenly really sharp.

nodes.label: F70-0032
nodes.text: the car drives well and is comfortable with plenty of space. i'm still getting my head around the technical features, mainly because i haven't been in the car much thanks to a health issue. i do like the stylish appearance of the car.

nodes.label: F70-0033
nodes.text: i absolutely love this car, it rides so smoothly and is really comfortable. the performance is terrific all round. it was always my dream car and still is, and it does not let me down in any part.

nodes.label: F70-0034
nodes.text:
easy car to drive and it gives a real sense of peace of mind.
improvements
the door pocket is slightly awkward to use, it is so deep things end up out of easy reach.

nodes.label: F70-0035
nodes.text: service at the beginning was excellent, but i was very disappointed that bmw took about a month to clear my previous finance, which meant i ended up making an extra payment. that extra payment has now been refunded, but if i had not chased to see why it still had not been settled as agreed, i do wonder how long it would have taken for anyone to notice.

nodes.label: F70-0036
nodes.text: there are far too many technical features added which feel unnecessary and possibly dangerous. it seems to have lost its way that it is meant to be a car. standard useful and necessary items have been taken away or need to be reset every time you start a journey.

nodes.label: F70-0037
nodes.text: i've already recommended my car to other people, but i don't think you should be charged extra for subscription features that would barely get used, like the silly games. i'm really not pleased with the after sales support, it felt basically non existent, and honestly, if you asked me right now if i'd go back to bmw, my answer would be no.

nodes.label: F70-0038
nodes.text: lots of power packed into a small body

nodes.label: F70-0039
nodes.text: the compact size, strong performance, and the more sophisticated overall form.

nodes.label: F70-0040
nodes.text: very good car with excellent driving performance, but i'm disappointed there's no split or individual front seat aircon and no central control for the rear seats like my old 1 series had.

nodes.label: F70-0041
nodes.text: i do really like the car, but i think some connected drive features like spotify and the better maps should be included as standard rather than extra.

nodes.label: F70-0042
nodes.text: this 1 series is my first ever bmw and i'm really impressed with the power, the fuel economy and how comfortable it is. the amount of standard kit is great, and the safety features make me feel confident and are a big help, especially when parking. the seats are extremely comfortable and the cabin is very quiet, so it is a very enjoyable car to drive. the materials used inside feel high quality and the os9 instruments are very detailed with lots of different display options. i would happily recommend the 1 series and i expect to stay with bmw for many years.

nodes.label: F70-0043
nodes.text: ideal-sized car for town driving with a really cracking engine

nodes.label: F70-0044
nodes.text: its compact but comfy to ride in and really easy to drive

nodes.label: F70-0045
nodes.text: i used to own an m135i, and that one was much more fun to drive, mainly because the exhaust sounded fantastic. the new m135 has almost no sound and feels boring to drive, even though the new interior is really well done.

nodes.label: F70-0046
nodes.text: i have been running bmw cars for close to 50 years, both new and used, for personal use and for work. before choosing the 120 i looked very closely at almost every rival in the same price bracket and simply couldnt find a reason not to go for the 120. the spec, the quality and the service are just better than the rest.

nodes.label: F70-0047
nodes.text: the driving feel is good, but the software is terrible, the car acts like it has its own mind and starts doing things for no clear reason. very inconsistent behavior. i absolutely hate it!!

nodes.label: F70-0048
nodes.text: this is now my 3rd bmw and i've genuinely loved every single one of them. in my view bmw offers the best customer service and overall experience, not just at the point of buying the car but throughout the whole ownership journey. that's a big part of why i chose to come back again and why i'm on my 3rd bmw, and it's also why i'd happily recommend bmw to anyone.

nodes.label: F70-0049
nodes.text: i'm very pleased with the car, though it could feel a little more engaging, but given my last car was a v8 m3 that's probably not a fair benchmark. i am however totally disappointed with the insurance setup, as the 5 day pick up insurance was never activated by the dealer, and even after raising it with you there's been no satisfactory reply. at this point i feel going to the regulator might be the only route.

nodes.label: F70-0050
nodes.text: there is a weird droning sound coming from the rear on the drivers side, and it has been there since i picked it up from the showroom. the demo car i tried before, same model, did not have that noise. the dealer is still trying to find another demo car so they can see if this is normal for the model or just my particular vehicle.

nodes.label: F70-0051
nodes.text: great car, good looks, handles nicely

nodes.label: F70-0052
nodes.text: this is my fourth brand new bmw. this version is quite a departure from my old 118i m sport and has lost a number of refinements that used to come as standard, which is a let-down. even so, i'd still score it 10 because of the solid bmw enginering.

nodes.label: F70-0053
nodes.text: the best car i have ever driven

nodes.label: F70-0054
nodes.text:
the mild hybrid start feels subtle.
there are too many separate safety systems.
frequent stops when refueling. etc

nodes.label: F70-0055
nodes.text: service has been fine and the car itself is good. the only issue is the creasing on the front alcantara seats, both driver and passenger, they really dont look up to the level of the seats in my earlier bmw cars. i am already in touch with the dealer about this problem and hoping that, if it turns out to be a design fault, it will get sorted out.

nodes.label: F70-0056
nodes.text: very good-looking car, modern interior with features that fit that modern style.

nodes.label: F70-0057
nodes.text: suspension feels overly firm, lots of passengers mention it.

nodes.label: F70-0058
nodes.text: the ride is supposed to be comfortable, and it mostly is. however, i felt the sunlight ought to be reduced a bit more.

nodes.label: F70-0059
nodes.text: great fuel economy with really comfortable ride quality

nodes.label: F70-0060
nodes.text:
it does not go as far as the f20 design, but the nose is longer for ff than before.
advanced tech curved display (10 if you don't have this sos once blacked out)
10 if you don't have this light safety first or can't switch it off

nodes.label: F70-0061
nodes.text: it is frustrating that with each new bmw 1 series i own, fewer things seem to come as standard. putting spotify, satellite view and other functions behind a paid premium subscription is just poor.

nodes.label: F70-0062
nodes.text: i really hate that the car keeps trying to tell me how i should drive. on top of that, the information and communications don't explain the product in a straightforward way. and the extras that other premium brands include as standard just feel like a complete rip off.

nodes.label: F70-0063
nodes.text: good-looking car, comfortable with strong performance and decent equipment.

nodes.label: F70-0064
nodes.text: very happy with it - simple to drive, comfy and with good functionality.

nodes.label: F70-0065
nodes.text: i'm happy with all aspects of it, but the cost keeps me from telling everyone to get one

nodes.label: F70-0066
nodes.text: this car fits my daily needs perfectly.great fun to drive, very comfortable, stylish and looks amazing, it gets plenty of remarks all of them good & on top of that the hybrid setup is even better than i imagined. this is my 8th bmw & while i was very pleased with the other seven this one really goes further. fuel economy is also even better than i wished for.

nodes.label: F70-0067
nodes.text: it drives well, with excellent acceleration!!

nodes.label: F70-0068
nodes.text: solidly built car with up-to-date technology. as a pensioner i would have preferred to have a hard copy user manual.

nodes.label: F70-0069
nodes.text: car itself is really excellent, just let down by the new tech system being way too complicated.

nodes.label: F70-0070
nodes.text: great car, good value, pleased with everything excellent service from bmw bristol, staff are knowledgeable and professional. chris who sold me the car is very helpful but not too pushy, he was the reason i bought it. alex in sales very helpful too. very happy with the car.

nodes.label: F70-0071
nodes.text: great driving performance, nice styling and good fuel economy.

nodes.label: F70-0072
nodes.text: I had a 118i m sport before and the 120 m sport has had all the useful bits stripped out and is not a sport model at all! this is our 6th bmw and easily the worst car we've ever had. 1. no 12v socket in the boot, a ridiculous penny pinching move. 2. no phone charging points in the back. 3. no climate controls in the rear. 4. no fog lights. 5. no leather seats. 6. no visible exhaust, sport model?? 7. basic 18" alloys (19" were standard on the 118i), sport model?? 8. thin, cheap carpets with poor grip and no m sport trim. every one of these came standard on the 118i m sport and the 120 m sport is marketed as its direct replacement! the 120 m sport is about £7/8k more, plus paying again for all the things removed, making it a pricey car and the worst thing ever to come out of a bmw showroom. total rubbish!

nodes.label: F70-0073
nodes.text: this car doesnt really bring any new special offering... the older version felt more purposeful

nodes.label: F70-0074
nodes.text: even with the easy handling, you still really feel the fun that comes from riding a bmw.

nodes.label: F70-0075
nodes.text: really nice car to drive and it looks great as well. first time i have had an automatic and i am enjoying that a lot.

nodes.label: F70-0076
nodes.text: the size and the way it handles feel spot on, and its running performance is the best. it fits 5 people, and i think it is the best option as long as you are ok with the firm ride and not taking big luggage.

nodes.label: F70-0077
nodes.text: i want a sports car that not many people are in. the m135 has excellent performance, but it does not feel ahead of other cars.

nodes.label: F70-0078
nodes.text: the car went back to the dealer on 12th october 2024 for inspection because one headlamp had constant moisture inside. we were told a replacement would take about 2 weeks to arrive. we are still waiting for our car to come back. weve only been able to enjoy this brand new bmw, one of the first f70 1 series in the uk, for 6 weeks out of 17 weeks of owning it! this is really upsetting and not acceptable. bmw uk are aware of what is going on but we still have no date for when we will get the car back.

nodes.label: F70-0079
nodes.text: it feels nice when running

nodes.label: F70-0080
nodes.text: great motorcar, stylish with a quality drvie

nodes.label: F70-0081
nodes.text: over roughly the last 15 years ive had a new 1 series each time, and every version has got better. the 123 is the best yet, x drive has definitely improved the road holding and the petrol consumption is excellent. i feel the air conditioning controls should be manual, same for the sat nav. the wheel design needs changing as theyre a real nuisance to clean, just like the front grill. apart from that its a first class car and im already looking forward to my next bmw in around 2.5 years.

nodes.label: F70-0082
nodes.text: it feels small and easy to handle, and it comes nicely equiped, but the suspension is way too hard.

nodes.label: F70-0083
nodes.text: it was really nice getting regular updates from the contract stage right through to delivery.

nodes.label: F70-0084
nodes.text: because its autonomous driving feels quite complete.

nodes.label: F70-0085
nodes.text: after my husband changed his phone he has not been able to load the bmw app, and even though he has asked for help he just keeps getting passed around. on the day we collected the car it was not ready because they had sprayed the roof black as they could not secure the car we had been promised. we did not get a proper hand over as we were anxious about picking up primary schoolchildren and had told the garage we would have to go. about 5 or 6 weeks later we needed an emergency technician and the car had to return to the garage because the gps in the roof fin had been damaged by rain, so the roof was resprayed. now in feb we still do not have the car we originally ordered and are waiting for a part for the black grill it should have had. the new manager martin has been trying to sort things out. we had other problems too but i am running out of spa.

nodes.label: F70-0086
nodes.text: i find the constant speed alert annoying, having to switch it off every single time i get in. at night the dash doesnt light up the vent position controls, and the lights at the end of the dash reflect in the side windows, getting in the way of the view in the door mirrors. the car really ought to have electric tailgate controls as standard.

nodes.label: F70-0087
nodes.text: very good value to run, since it can use the cheapest diesel while petrol prices keep rising. the strong acceleration makes it really fun to drive.

nodes.label: F70-0088
nodes.text: i really like the car overall, but having only a full touch screen with no physical buttons is irritating and quite distracting. after just a few months the touch screen already feels slow. the buttons on the previous model were far better and much easier to operate.

nodes.label: F70-0089
nodes.text: i really enjoy driving this new car, the pickup is faster and there is none of the lag the last model had. the boost button has been very handy when joining the a12 with its short run in.

nodes.label: F70-0090
nodes.text: i cant play music from a usb flash drive, and android auto is awkward to use.

nodes.label: F70-0091
nodes.text: really like this car, it rides comfortably, has good fuel economy and is fun to drive. plenty of space with decent leg room in the back seats.

nodes.label: F70-0092
nodes.text: because the auto drive worked well

nodes.label: F70-0093
nodes.text: we run two cars at the moment, the new bmw and a 6 year old mini countryman 2 litre petrol. i actually like the countryman much more, so much so that if i could have bought a new like for like countryman i would have gone for that instead of the bmw. it is far more comfortable, nicer to drive and easily quick enough, with not a huge gap in mpg between them. the dials and controls are more old school on the countryman but i find them simpler to use and they give everything a driver needs. ideally i would keep my 6 year old mini and also have a brand new one with the same specification rather than the bmw. despite that i am still generally a fan of bmw. happy to talk about it further. mark benson.

nodes.label: F70-0094
nodes.text: the fundamental performance of the car is spot on. the people at the dealership are excellent, both on the sales side and in service. the downside is that older people have a hard time figuring out how the different applications and functions work. after an update, the settings i had made, like the automatic parking brake feature and my mobile phone registration, were all reset.

nodes.label: F70-0095
nodes.text: i changed from the 3 series because of the parking space, but even though this is smaller and narrower it doesn't feel tight inside, and it is quick on its feet and has enough power. i really liked the instrument panel design, it looks upscale and is easy to read. i chose the m sport and i'm also pleased with the suspension and the audio. i think it is recommendable for people who want good fuel economy and do not like driving something big.

nodes.label: F70-0096
nodes.text: i have had this one for about three months now, but i still don't really remember the feeling of sliding in the same model as before. what stands out is how simple it is to control and how it can cruise calmly even when i'm going fast. the price of the car itself feels quite high though. i picked this model because i was willing to pay more in order to get a comfortable drive. originally i chose a 116i f20 for my wife, and the steering on that is outstanding, you can really sense what the driver is feeling. after that, i bought a lexus is as a replacement for a 435i and that was excellent too. then came the 116i m135, which is also strong in power and easy to manage, and now i'm on an x3m competition. i use the m135 around town and the x3mc when i'm going at high speeds.

nodes.label: F70-0097
nodes.text: it's a lovely car, but i'm really annoyed that the latest system update stopped auto hold from staying on, so now i have to switch it back on every single trip.

nodes.label: F70-0098
nodes.text: it drives nicely and stays quiet. it comes with full equipment. the controls are simple to handle. fuel efficiency is very good. i enjoy being behind the wheel. i also appreciate the design.

nodes.label: F70-0099
nodes.text: simple to handle around city streets

nodes.label: F70-0100
nodes.text:
- while driving, the interior light randomly comes on and can only be switched off via the screen.
- a few times the radio station name has suddenly stopped showing.
- bluetooth can disconnect out of nowhere.
- if the car sits unused for around a week, the rear mirror ends up tilted down.

nodes.label: F70-0101
nodes.text: this car has been a total let down. if i could get my old 2021 m135i back i would be far happier. the apps and drive modes are overly complex, not user friendly at all, and far too distracting and difficult to use while driving, so you basically have to stop to deal with them. the way it handles is like a boat in a storm, no matter which drive setting you choose, and it is definitely not a sport hatch. the driving sound is too fake, the interior feels cheap, and a lot of practical conveniences have disappeared. there is no storage box on the driver side of the dash and no 12v socket in the boot. the m sport seats now lack support and comfort, unlike the previous standard version of those seats. after 3 months in this i am already looking to swap to another car. it is the worst car change i have made, not an improvement at all, and a big regrettable mistake.

nodes.label: F70-0102
nodes.text: we have owned bmws for many years, so we are disappointed with our latest 120i m sport, first registered april 2025. we added extra optional kit on top of the standard packages. we have made numerous calls to the dealership about the exterior door handle lighting that is fitted, as we cannot get it programmed and the dealer says they cannot assist. we have found a matching 2025 car without the comfort package where the handles have no lights at all, which makes me think our lights were never coded from new. we have also seen, in certain sunlight, tiny speckles across the front windscreen. we asked about this and were told the dealer needs to view it, but for reasons beyond our control we have not managed to go. we will look forward to your reply.

nodes.label: F70-0103
nodes.text: i like my new car, but i would much rather have a paper manual. having it in an app on my phone or ipad or on the car screen is ok, yet its just easier to check an index and a page number in a book.

nodes.label: F70-0104
nodes.text: because the fuel consumption turned out worse than i expecetd.

nodes.label: F70-0105
nodes.text: i reckon people will either like it or not like it, so pick someone specific to recomend it to.

nodes.label: F70-0106
nodes.text: for the money, the bmw 120 feels like an incredible amount of car, with comfort and driving enjoyment you usually link to much bigger models. i am hugely impressed and really very pleased with the choice i made!

nodes.label: F70-0107
nodes.text:
being able to do tight turns is convenient.
its compact size is fine even in the long run
gas mileage is good.

nodes.label: F70-0108
nodes.text: really enjoyable to drive, performance is excellent, exactly what you expect from bmw

nodes.label: F70-0109
nodes.text: very good fuel economy

nodes.label: F70-0110
nodes.text: brakes have awful progression when trying to creep forward in a car park, they feel jerky and not smooth like any other auto i have owned, which is very annoying. the passenger seatbelt keeps knocking when it is not being used. i also think it is ridiculous that extra features cost more, shame on you bmw. on the positive side it does drive better than my last car.

nodes.label: F70-0111

overall the car is good, but my score drops because of a few things:
* the xdrive feels too front-wheel biased. a rear-wheel bias would have suited it better and been more fun, especially since this is supposed to be a semi-enthusiast car with 300hp and a price around 500 tkr.
* there are shift paddles instead of a proper gear lever. even a sequential "fake" shift lever for the dct would have felt better than paddles. the paddles come across as a gimmick and really only make sense on the highway. when you are turning or trying to drift, the paddles are basically useless.
* there are no physical controls for climate comfort like ac or seat heating. the screen is extremely clunky for the things you change all the time, such as temperature. for everything else, the screen works great.
* the software is buggy. sometimes the infotainment and the dashboard freeze and i have to restart them by pressing and holding the volume scroll buton.
i honestly wouldnt have gone for this car if it werent for the excellent leasing offer, about 4500 sek per month for 2 years. the choice was between leasing this or buying an old tuned volvo 740. i am happy i picked this one, but when you want to have fun driving, the gear paddles and the slightly too strong front-wheel bias do make it feel a bit limited.

i sent this over to the gm at skyline bmw and still haven't heard back.
dear jordan merrick,
i recently bought a new bmw 530i from skyline bmw, expecting a premium experience that fits the brand's reputation. instead, what happened has raised some serious concerns that i feel need attention.
a few days after taking delivery, i noticed a scuff on the front headlight and paint chips on the hood. when i told my sales rep, he said they would take care of it. when i brought the car back, the paint chips were touched up, but the scuff on the headlight was still there. when i pointed that out, i was told the dealership does a pre-delivery inspection, basically suggesting the damage couldn't have been there before i bought it.
while i understand new cars go through inspections, i have reason to suspect my vehicle might have been used by someone else prior to my purchase. the car already had over 120 miles on it when i bought it, and when i connected my phone to apple carplay, i found that another device had been registered before.
because of all this, i don't feel sure that i actually received a brand-new vehicle in the condition i expected. i purchased this car for my business and had been planning on additional vehicles for my family, but this situation has made me question that decision.
i believe resolving this in a fair and professional way would reflect well on your dealership and help rebuild my confidence in your focus on customer satisfaction. it would not only restore my trust, but also reinforce my thinking about future purchases for my wife and daughter. excellent service stands out, and i am more than willing to share a positive story if this is handled properly.
please let me know how we can address this matter at your earliest convenience. i look forward to hearing from you.
regards,
marcus delaine
delaine capital, llc

nodes.text:
my first experience with a bmw 7 series was as a passenger back in the early 2000s, and it really left a lasting impression on me. that memory stayed with me and eventually led to buying my first bmw 7 series around 2008. a few years later, i traded that car in for something more suited to family needs, but the feeling of driving a bmw never left. i promised myself i would own another bmw someday.
that time is now, and i'm extremely happy with my 2025 bmw 540i xdrive. the excitement i felt in my early 20s is exactly what i feel again in my early 40s, and even more so. the overall bmw experience is special: the comfort, the ride, the styling, and the distinct personality of the 540i xdrive make it unforgettable.
there are, however, a couple of areas that could be improved. first, the front-facing camera. i get why it's positioned where it is, but aesthetically the placement isn't appealing. from the side, it really sticks out and makes you wonder why it couldn't have been put somewhere more subtle. the bump disrupts the smooth, clean lines of the front bumper. second, the front driver and passenger usb-c charging ports are awkwardly placed. you really have to shift your body noticeably to plug in properly, and a more convenient location would be much better.
all that said, i'm thrilled every time i get behind the wheel of my 540i xdrive and plan to enjoy it for many years.

nodes.text:
overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.
range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.
on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.
seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.
cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.
in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.
and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

all of my earlier bmws were bought new and then swapped out for another one in under 4 years, in this order:

run flat tires mostly gone and no spare?
1) putting a 4 cylinder motor in any 5 series

5) ventilated seats fan seems weaker, airflow reduced

7) everything is "touch" instead of "press". i would rather have push buttons for lock/unlock or some audible lock/unlock feedback.
8) windshield washer fluid coming through the wipers, which often clog, instead of separate exterior spray points.
those are some problems with the car itself. i also have customer service and process concerns with the austin tx dealership on lakeshore rd.
my current 530 was bought from horizon automotive in san antonio. my previous 4 bmws came from trailway automotive group in austin.
i was handled badly and very unprofessionally by trailway in austin when i tried to buy there again this time. i have always lived in san antonio but had chosen to purchase in austin until that last experience.

nodes.text:
from a mechanical standpoint the car is excellent, in line with what i've come to expect from my previous seven bmws. it drives smooth, is very quiet and feels luxurious.
all of the problems i've run into are tied to the software.
route planning -
there is room to improve the in-car navigation system.
1-you are unable to plan a charging route starting from anywhere other than where the vehicle is currently parked, and you cannot set a starting charge level different from the present state of charge. that makes it impossible to pre-plan the second leg of a longer trip. this information should be something you can input.
2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.
4-route planning on bmwusa.com is basically useless. try it. choose range and route, i7 e50 20", put in a starting point like 210 harbor view rd, seaview beach fl and a destination like lakeside toyota of fairview. the result is just a line on the map with state names. no city labels. no identified charging stops. nothing that actually helps an ev driver. on a previous attempt it also showed a "?" button that, when pressed, only told me i would need to charge somewhere on the way. that is not helpful.
5-i ended up having to build a spreadsheet and use my own numbers to plan the journey. i've asked the local "genius" for guidance, but the way bmw's supporting software is designed is beyond what she can assist with.
6-i'm still hoping the mistakes are mine and that you can show me a better way to use these tools. but as i see things right now, the limitations of bmw's route planing tools aren't just unhelpful - they feel insulting. maybe that would be borderline acceptable in an economy car, but not in the i7.
seat positioning -
most of the time, after i unlock, get in, start the car and buckle up, the driver's seat moves correctly from the comfort access spot to the stored position 1 for driving. however, roughly 20% of the time it doesn't move at all. and once it even slid further back instead. usually tapping the "1" button will fix it, but sometimes that button has to be held down, and sometimes only the seat controls on the door will get it to move. i suspect there might be some link to how and when i clear the nuisance disclaimer message.
updates -
not long ago i was away for about a week. the first time i drove the car after coming back, i found a lot of things had been reset. my seat memories had vanished. the custom wake word i'd set was no longer active. saying "hey bmw" did nothing, even though those options still showed as selected in the menus. there were also new displays in the instrument cluster when driving with assist plus.
it would help if:
1 - existing user settings were kept intact when an update is installed.
2-a simple message popped up at startup letting the driver know the vehicle might behave differently than it did on the last drive.
thank you for looking at my comments on this car. it's unfortunate that these frustrations exist. out of all the bmws i've owned, this is the one i am most eager to drive.
i would really like to get a response to the issues i've mentioned.
mark ellis
[EMAIL]

Update from roughly 2/5/25:
his overall experience with this vehicle so far has been poor. the car has been tied up in service for around 24 days. when the vehicle only had about 100 miles, the Check Engine Light came on for the first time. his service technician believed the concern was related to the O2 sensors. when the dealership contacted BMW engineering for support, engineering did not want to approve replacing those sensors at that stage and instead told service to clear the fault codes and have the customer drive the car more to see if the Check Engine Light would return. the light did in fact come back on, and he then had to bring the vehicle back into the service department. he ended up driving about 800 extra miles with the Check Engine Light illuminated. eventually service replaced the O2 sensors to resolve the issue. they were also told the vehicle might require a software update if the Check Engine Light comes back again. the way BMW handled the troubleshooting has been very frustrating and that BMW needs to listen more closely to what the technician on the ground is recommending. the second trip into service could have been avoided if BMW had listened to the technician who was diagnosing the car the first time. he has had the car back for about a week and it is running OK, but he is still worried the check engine light might reappear. nodes.text:
it is an excellent car in terms of ride comfort, steering feel, braking and the basics, but there are several "features" that make using it somewhat unpleasant.
1) with the car in drive, the doors will still open if someone accidentally touches the door open button. this feels dangerous. that function really ought to be disabled whenever the vehicle is in gear. and honestly, why have power opening doors at all when simple manual door handles have worked perfectly for roughly the last century.
2) the interior manual door release handles are positioned in places that are very hard to reach.
3) the auto stop-start turns the engine off before the car is fully stopped. in stop-and-go traffic this is irritating and inconvenient because you lose engine braking as soon as the engine shuts down.
4) there is no way to defeat the auto stop-start in the normal drive mode. i know using sport mode avoids this, but i do not want to drive around in sport mode.
5) the engine automatically switches off when you put the transmission in park and open the driver door. this is a hassle when briefly stopping to let a passenger out and then continuing the trip.
6) the horn will blast loudly while the car is in park if the driver steps out with the key to open the trunk or similar. i really dislike being yelled at by the car.
7) the front passenger seat slides backward toward the rear passenger as they open their door to get out, which makes it harder for them to exit. comfort exit is turned off in the settings, yet this still happens.
8) the driver seat moves backward and then instantly forward again when the transmission is put in park and the seatbelt unlatched, even though comfort exit is disabled in the seat menu.
9) the sharp, perforated metal grilles over the door speakers have led to several passengers and drivers snagging and breaking fingernails while feeling around for the door panel buttons.
10) there is no way to close the trunk lid from inside the cabin.
i am assuming other drivers have raised the same complaints and that bmw can deal with at least some of them soon with a software update. of course, the locations of the door release handles and speaker grilles would need a physical redesign.
michael doran
lead chauffeur
fairmont holdings
[PHONE]

1-interior:
a-warm air isn't really warm enough and takes too long to build up. i have to put the temperature on max just to feel actual warmth.
b-the seats have plenty of adjustment options, but overall they are not very comfortable. maybe that's partly personal, but there should still be a default seat comfort you can expect at this level.
c-a rear-seat display should be standard at this price, not an extra-cost upgrade, especially nowadays when an oled screen is around 200$ for a consumer. if the motorization around it makes it pricey, that part should be the added cost.
d-the glossy trim shows fingerprints far too easily, and since everything is touch sensitive it's difficult to wipe it clean without accidentally changing settings.
2-driving experience:
a-for a car of this size, the steering feels a bit too wide. rear wheel steering seems like something that should be default for a premium vehicle like this.
b-overall the car is too needy, constantly popping up notifications, which can be distracting. the red light warning is not well tuned, as it will alert me even on the highway when it spots the signal for the entrance lane on the right. that is very distracting and frankly a bug.
c-switching out of autopilot isn't smooth enough, and the car behaves a bit stubborn. sometimes it decides to change lane at a very bad moment. for instance, if the navigation says i need to take an exit in under a mile, it shouldn't try to move into the opposite lane just to go faster.
d-the autopilot braking is quite harsh. even when it clearly detects the car ahead slowing, it reduces speed too late, making the brakes feel very strong.

nodes.text:
my i7 has been an absolutely fantastic car so far, and the way it drives has felt perfect to me. it is extremely comfortable, and the overall quietness of the drivetrain and cabin is beyond what i have experienced with similar cars i owned before. the tech and amenities in the i7 meet or even surpass what i expect in this class. everyone who has ridden with me has been impressed with these same things. the range does drop in the winter, but for my daily use i find the range acceptable.
my only real issue with this particular car is that it arrived with bubbles in the sunroof glass, and the dealer is currently working on it. the car has been diagnosed with a manufacturer defect in the sunroof, with several small bubbles trapped between the glass layers of the panel. i am worried these imperfections could weaken the sunroof and affect safety over time, especially with temperature changes or impacts from rough or uneven roads. the team at bmw of Fairview has been great throughout all of this, showing professionalism, being transparent, and keeping me thoroughly informed while they resolve it. the problem, however, means the car needs a major teardown and repair, including removing the interior headliner, the pillar trim, the sun shade cassette, the windshield, and the driver assistance camera assembly, etc. since i have only had the car a few months, it is extremely frustrating to deal with such a big problem so early in ownership. i have barely had time to really enjoy what was supposed to be a flagship, brand-new vehicle before finding out it has to be significantly dismantled to fix this. as a long-time bmw fan and repeat owner, i have always respected the brand for its quality, precision, and innovation.
to date, the i7 has genuinely been a joy to own. in every other way it has met and even exceeded what i expect from a flagship executive sedan. the level of craftsmanship, the outstanding comfort, and the excellent noise isolation make each trip calm and very refined, which is exactly what i associate with bmw and the idea of the "ultimate driving machine." that makes this problem even more disheartening, since i expected years of worry-free enjoyment and trust in the car. with such a quiet cabin and electric drivetrain, i now fear that an invasive repair like this might never bring the car fully back to its original, factory-perfect state, and could introduce new shakes or rattles later.

i have a 750e 2026, and this is my second 7 series model. from the very first day, the car has been making a repeating knocking sound from the right rear passenger side, very much like the automatic door lock noise (da-da). the dealership has been supportive, understanding, and professional while trying to track it down, and they have traced it to a valve that is supposed to push gas vapors toward the engine when a certain buildup level is reached.
this sound is distracting and extremely annoying to everyone in the car, and it happens while driving, when stopped, with a full tank, with a half tank, and so on. to me, that points to poor quality control on the manufacturer side, which is very disappointing. i highly doubt this is just a single isolated case and assume you have already heard about it. the 750e is marketed as your flagship, but with this issue it does not really feel like one, and i think it needs to be handled properly at the manufacturer level. i am also worried it could be a safety-related problem.
as a separate irritation, i would expect bmw to include safety features that even cheaper cars already have. specifically, there should be an optional audible alert for blind spot lane changes, in addition to the triangle symbol on the side mirrors. that triangle is hard to see, and a tone to warn that there is a vehicle in the lane would be very useful and much appreciated. make it an option that can be turned on or off, but at least offer it.
thank you for letting me share my disappointment; bmw management really should look into these matters. this is my third bmw, and i am starting to lose that pride in owning one. none of this is a criticism of my local dealership, they are always professional and supportive. honestly, without their effort to keep clients satisfied, i would most likely already be back in a mercedes. the dealer team truly acts like quintessential professionals and treats customers like family.
again, thanks for your time. you can reach out to me directly if you wish; coastal bmw - clearwater, fl has my contact information.
- david lane

while i actually prefer how the 7 series interior looks compared to the s class, i would still tell most family and friends to go with the s class instead, because of a mix of issues i've run into.
first, the premium audio: the top b&w setup is just so-so. for a "top of the line" system it doesn't stack up against the burmester premium system at all.
then the transmission behavior. when you really get on the throttle, the shifts in my 760i are noticeably rough. even my previous s63 amg, under heavy acceleration, shifted more smoothly than this car does.
the navigation software is another weak point. when driving in complicated road situations, it's not as intuitive or clear. it doesn't give enough early guidance for moving across several lanes on 6- or 8-lane city freeways, and it's not very clear about things like multi-lane exits where you need to pick a specific lane right after you exit. on top of that, the lane guidance is shown only in the hud, which feels like a bad design choice; those lane markers really should also show up on the main center display.
overall, the instrument screen behind the steering wheel is used poorly. both mercedes and audi handle that area much better, integrating it in a more sensible way with the center screen and hud, and audi especially is far ahead when it comes to how you can customize what's shown there.
the rear side window blinds are another disappointment, for two reasons. first, you have to go into the media screens to raise the shades, instead of them simply coming up automatically with a second press on the window raise hard button. second, the open channel where the side blinds sit looks unfinished. it comes across as unprofessional compared to what mercedes or audi do, where they have top covers hiding the blinds when they're stowed.
not being able to turn off auto start stop separately from the chosen drive mode is also annoying.
with the cruise control follow distance, there are two problems. you can't adjust the following gap while actually driving without digging through multiple menus, and even at the maximum setting the car follows too closely at moderate speeds. between about 45 and 60 mph, the farthest setting still feels uncomfortably, almost rudely, close to the car ahead.
the automatic lane keeping is behind the competition too. compared to audi and mercedes, it doesn't hold the lane as reliably or as smoothly, often failing to stay centered and tending to wander side to side. the lane keeping in this 760 really reminds me of mercedes' first generation system from something like 10 to 12 years ago.

2024 bmw 760i, to me, is a true mix of power and elegance. as a proud owner of the 2024 bmw 760i, it's hard not to be drawn in by how commanding it looks out on the road. the sleek exterior and the luxurious cabin make this flagship sedan feel like it radiates power and sophistication.
there's a real sense of empowerment that comes with driving something so prestigious. my wife, who is 5 foot 2 and around 100 pounds, is especially taken with the way the 760i carries itself. for her, it isn't just about the car's size, it's about feeling like she's in charge of the road and in control of a serious machine.
for her it goes beyond simple transportation; it's a statement, a way of showing her presence and capability. the 760i lives up to that, with strong performance from its potent engine and advanced tech features that give real confidence behind the wheel. whether we're weaving through city streets or cruising the highway, every trip feels like a small victory.
of course, people see a car like this differently. some might think it's about a "look-at-me" syndrome, wanting attention or validation. that may be true for some, but for many others a bmw 760i represents the result of hard work and success, a reward for what they've achieved and a symbol of personal accomplishment.
for me the 2024 bmw 760i is far more than just another vehicle; it stands for power, elegance and prestige. even if opinions about what it means vary, one thing is clear to me: it brings a huge amount of joy and satisfaction to anyone lucky enough to live with it every day.

even though i really love the car itself, my first experiences with it have made me nervous about what owning it long-term will be like. the very first thing that went wrong was a dead 48 volt battery right at vehicle pickup, which meant i couldn't even drive my new $150,000 car home. i ended up waiting about a week while they sourced and installed a new battery.
then at just under 3,000 miles the dcs module failed, which made the brakes almost useless and nearly caused me to be part of a several-car pileup on a local freeway. this happened on december 23rd, during a drive from palm desert to pasadena (roughly 130 miles), and that made it even harder to get a tow truck out to me since i was about 88 miles from home. the wait for the tow was something like 3+ hours.
i've now been in a dealership loaner for over 10 days because the part my car needed was discontinued and replaced by a newer version that still isn't available. i will say bmw emergency service and my service advisors have been responsive, understanding, and sympathetic.
this is my 9th bmw, so i'm familiar with the quirks and issues they tend to develop as they get older, but seeing big problems like this on a brand-new vehicle feels pretty disheartening and discouraging. i waited a long time to be able to buy what i thought was the pinnacle of the bmw lineup, and now that i finally did, i feel somewhat let down.
that said, i truly love the look, the feel, and the way this thing drives; it has met or even exceeded what i expected from a flagship bmw. i'm hopeful that as we go forward my trust in bmw and its craftsmanship will come back. thank you for letting me share all of this.
